evidence: gpt-oss: "adj[u] |= 1 << v" and "adj[v] |= 1 << u"; qwen: "adj[u].add(v)" and "adj[v].add(u)"; glm: "adj[u].add(v)" and "adj[v].add(u)"
affordance_in_statement: However, all such grievances result in a symmetric separation ... for each of the three possible pairs ... at least one log entry where one technician in the pair filed a grievance against the other.
secondary_shortcut_name: Guaranteed existence of a qualifying triad
removal_suggestion: Make qualification direction-sensitive: explicitly require that, for every pair, the lower-ID technician filed the grievance against the higher-ID technician; a reverse-direction report must not count. This preserves the shown examples but invalidates solutions that automatically add both directions.

survivor_shortcuts.affordance: all such grievances result in a symmetric separation

survivor_shortcuts.shortcut: Builds symmetric adjacency sets before searching for the lexicographically smallest triangle.
survivor_shortcuts.affordance: for each ... pair ... at least one log entry where one technician ... filed ... against the other

common_affordance: The directed grievance list can be collapsed into an undirected graph because separation is stated to be symmetric.

defeated_student_causes.why_failed: Its Python implementation scans all O(n^3) triples using a dense Boolean matrix, which is too slow at n = 2000.

recommended_edit: Replace the symmetric-pair condition with: "A pair qualifies only when the technician with the smaller ID filed a grievance against the technician with the larger ID; a grievance in the opposite direction does not qualify the pair."
regression_risk: This change could restore the already-defeated model only if its cubic scan happens to encounter a qualifying directed triangle quickly, but its worst-case TLE remains.
